<thought>The spectrum shows a strong M+2 peak at ~33% of the base peak, matching chlorine’s characteristic isotopic pattern (35Cl/37Cl ≈ 3:1). There is also a noticeable M+1 peak (~10% of base), consistent with the natural abundance of 13C in a molecule containing several carbons. No other element shows its distinctive isotopic signature (e.g., bromine’s ~1:1 M+2, sulfur’s low‑intensity M+2). Therefore, the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
